Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:10:1.english: Containers and cups - They are intentionally hidden, and he may not touch them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:10:2.hebrew: סכיני והמניק - שהן כלים קטנים, אבדה הן, שהשליכם שם עם האשפה שהוציאם מן הבית. ולקמן פריך: מאי שכן דרך אשפה לפנות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:10:2.english: Knives and a fork [hamnik] - Since they are small utensils, they are [considered] a lost item, for [the owner] threw them there with the garbage that he took out of the house. And later [the Gemara] asks: What is [meant by] "for such is the way of a garbage dump to be cleared"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:12:1.english: It is a deliberate loss - For he should have considered that they would clear it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:13:1.english: This is what [the baraita] teaches: because [it is] the way of a garbage dump to be cleared - For the owners decide to clear [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:13:2.english: To clear small utensils into it - from the house without [the owner's] knowledge.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:1.english: Found in a heap - A heap of stones from a wall that collapsed.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:2.english: These are his - [It is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:3.hebrew: מחציו ולחוץ - באחד מחורי כותל הסמוכים לרשות הרבים מצאה, מחצי עוביו של כותל ולחוץ, שלו, דאמרינן: אחד מבני רשות הרבים נתנו שם ושכח. דאע"ג דאמרן לעיל: ספק הינוח לא יטול, והאי הינוח הוא — הא מוקמי' למתני' בגמרא דשתיך טפי, דאיכא יאוש בעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:3.english: From its midpoint and outward - [If] he found it in one of the holes of the wall adjacent to the public domain, from half the thickness of the wall and outward, [it belongs] to him, for we say: one of the people of the public domain placed it there and forgot [it]. Even though we said above [that in a case of] uncertain placement one may not take [it], and this is [a case of] placement — behold, we establish the Mishnah in the Gemara [as referring to a case] where it is very rusted, so that there is despair of the owners.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:4.hebrew: ואפילו מצא בתוך הבית כו' - דלא ידוע דמאן נינהו, ובעליו נואשו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:14:4.english: And even [if] one found [them] inside the house, etc. - For it is not known whose they are, and their owners have despaired [of recovering them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:15:1.english: [A Tanna] taught - Regarding a heap [of rubble] and an old wall.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:15:2.english: That he can say to him - To the owner of the heap or to the owner of the wall.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:15:3.english: Of the Amorites - [They] were [of the Amorites] whom our forefathers dispossessed.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:15:4.hebrew: ישראל לא מצנעי - ומחציו ולפנים, אמאי שלו? הרי בעל הבית זה משתמש בה זה כמה שנים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:15:4.english: Jews do not conceal [items] - And from its midpoint inward, why is it his? Behold, this homeowner has been using it for many years.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:1:1.hebrew: כאבני בית קוליס - מרקוליס, והיא שם ע"ז, ולקמיה מפ' היכי עבדי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:1:1.english: Like the stones of Beit Kulis - Markulis, which is the name of an idol, and later [the Gemara] explains how they do [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:2:1.english: One here and one there - And the third [is] half on this one and half on that one.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:3:1.english: It is Neronian - Nero Caesar is written on it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:4:1.english: [If] one found behind a gafah [or behind a fence] bound fledglings - Gafah [is] a closing of a wall of wood or of reeds.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:4:3.hebrew: לא יגע בהן - טעמא מפ' בגמרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:4:3.english: He may not touch them - The reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:4:4.hebrew: מכוסה לא יגע בו - דאין זו אבידה שיהא מוזהר עליה בלא תוכל להתעלם, דמשתמר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:4:4.english: [If it is] covered, he may not touch it - For this is not a lost item regarding which he is cautioned by [the verse] "you may not ignore [it]," since it is guarded.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:7:1.english: Where [they] hop - from place to place.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:7:2.hebrew: מעלמא אתו - ואין זה הינוח, וכיון דאין בהן סימן, נימא: הרי אלו שלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:7:2.english: They came from elsewhere - and this is not [a case of] placing [them there], and since they have no distinguishing mark, let us say: behold, these are his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:1.english: And it can be said [that] a person concealed them - Since they are tied together.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:2.hebrew: ספק הינוח - בדבר שאין בו סימן, וכ"ש ודאי הינוח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:2.english: Uncertainty [as to] placement - [This refers to] an item that has no identifying mark, and all the more so [to] definite placement.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:3.hebrew: לכתחילה לא יטול - דאי שקלת לה, ליכא למרייהו סימנין למיתב בהו ויפסיד. הלכך, לא יטול, והבעלים יזכרו ויבאו ויטלום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:3.english: Ab initio he may not take [it] - For if you take it, their owners have no distinguishing marks to give for them, and [the owner] will suffer a loss. Therefore, he should not take [it], and the owners will remember and come and take them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:8:4.english: And if he took [it], he need not return [it] - For there is no one who can give an identifying mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:9:1.hebrew: שכן דרך אשפה ליפנות - ואי לא שקיל ליה האי השתא, לכשיפנה יטלנה נכרי או ישראל חשוד. הלכך, אבידה היא ומוזהר עליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 25b:9:1.english: Because it is routine for a garbage dump to be cleared - And if this [finder] does not take it now, when it is cleared, a gentile or a suspect Jew will take it. Therefore, it is a lost item, and he is enjoined concerning it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:1:1.hebrew: כאבני בית קוליס - מכאן אר"ת דאין שם ע"ז מרקוליס אלא קוליס, כדאמרינן הכא. והא דקרי ליה בעלמא מרקוליס — היינו חילוף קילוס, דהם קורים קילוס לשון שבח, וחכמים החליפו לגנאי, לשון "לעג וקלס" (תהלים מד); ו"מר" הוא חילוף, כמו "מר דשחוטה" דפרק גיד הנשה (חולין דף צד.), ו"מר דפרזלא" דהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיג:):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:1:1.english: Like the stones of Beit Kulis - From here Rabbeinu Tam says that the name of the idol is not Markulis [Mercury], but rather Kulis, as we say here. And the reason it is called Markulis elsewhere is [that it is] a substitute for kilus — for they call it kilus, an expression of praise, and the Sages changed it to [a term of] disparagement, an expression of "scorn and derision" (Psalms 44[:14]); and mar means substitute, like "mar of a slaughtered [bird]" in the chapter Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 94a), and "mar of iron" in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 113b).

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:4:1.hebrew: אחר הגפה - מקום שמשתמרות קצת. אבל מצא במקום שאין משתמר כלל, ודאי אבידה היא, ונתייאשו הבעלים כיון שאין בה סימן. ולא מיירי הכא במשתמר לגמרי, מדפריך בגמרא: "ולהוי קשר סימן", כלומר: ויטול ויכריז; ובמקום המשתמר, אפי' יש בו סימן — לא יגע בו, דהא תנן: מצא כלי טמון באשפה לא יגע בו, וביש בו סימן מיירי, מדקאמר: "ואם מגולה — נוטל ומכריז". וכן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף כד.) אמר: מצא אבידה, אם רוב ישראל — חייב להכריז, א"כ ביש בה סימן מיירי, ומוקי לה בטמון באשפה ונמלך עליה לפנותה, אבל אם לא נמלך — לא יגע בה. ולרבא דאמר: מקום הוי סימן, נקט דוקא גוזלות דמדדין, אבל דבר אחר — לא, דהוי מקום סימן ויטול ויכריז, כיון דאינו משתמר לגמרי. ולרבה דאמר: מקום לא הוי סימן, נקט גוזלות לאשמועינן דאע"ג דהוי ספק הינוח, דאיכא למימר דמעלמא אתו — לא יגע בהן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:4:1.english: Behind the wooden fence - [This refers to] a place where they are somewhat guarded. However, if one found [an item] in a place that is not guarded at all, it is certainly a lost item, and the owners have despaired [of recovering it] since it has no identifying mark. And [the Mishnah] is not speaking here of [a place] that is completely guarded, [as proven] from the fact that the Gemara objects: "Let the knot be an identifying mark," meaning, let him take [them] and proclaim [the find]; whereas in a [completely] guarded place, even if it has an identifying mark — he may not touch it, for we learned in the Mishnah: "If one found a vessel buried in a garbage dump, he may not touch it," and it is speaking of [a vessel] that has an identifying mark, [as proven] from what it states: "and if it is exposed, he takes [it] and proclaims [the find]." And similarly above (Bava Metzia 24a), [the Gemara] stated: [If] one found a lost item, if the majority [of the inhabitants] are Israelites, he is obligated to proclaim [it] — thus it is speaking of [an item] that has an identifying mark — and [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to [a vessel] buried in a garbage dump where [the owner] changed his mind about it to clear it out; however, if he did not change his mind, he may not touch it. And according to Rava, who says [that] location is an identifying mark, [the Mishnah] specifically chose fledglings because they hop [from place to place], whereas [for] another item — no, for the location is an identifying mark, and he takes [it] and proclaims [the find], since [the place] is not completely guarded. And according to Rabbah, who says [that] location is not an identifying mark, [the Mishnah] chose fledglings to teach us that even though it is a case of uncertain placement — since it can be said that they came from elsewhere — he may not touch them.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:8:1.hebrew: ואמר ר' אבא בר זבדא אמר רב ספק הינוח לכתחילה לא יטול - כדמפרש לעיל, דלמא איניש אצנעינהו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Zavda says [that] Rav says: [In a case of] uncertainty [as to] placement, ab initio one may not take [it] - As [the Gemara] explains above: perhaps a person concealed them.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:8:2.hebrew: ואם נטל לא יחזיר - יש מפרש דהיינו דוקא כשנטלהו והוליכו לביתו, דיש לחוש שמא באו בעלים בתוך כך ולא מצאו מה שהניחו שם, ושוב לא יחזרו לבקשה; לכך לא יחזיר למקום שנטל. אבל אם נטלו ולא זז משם, וראה שלא באו בעלים בתוך כך, יחזיר. וכן יש בירושלמי עובדא ברבי אבא בר זבדא גופיה, דקאמר: רבי אבא בר זבדא אשכח חמרא מכוסה בחפיסה ונסביה. אתא ושאיל בבי רב; אמרו ליה: לאו יאות עבדת. אמר להו: אהדריה? א"ל: לא, דלמא אתא מריה ולא אשכחיה, ומיאש מיניה. ומיהו "אם נטל לא יחזיר" משמע רק שנטלה, ואע"ג דלא הוליכה לשום מקום — לא יחזיר. ויש לפרש דמיירי הכא בספק אבידה, דאפי' הניחה בעלים שם מדעת, דומה ששכחוהו; דבלא משתמר כ"א קצת מיירי, דומיא דמתני', דעל מתני' קאי רבי אבא. ולכך "אם נטל לא יחזיר", דהשתא אבידה היא ושכחוה הבעלים; וכיון שאם היה יודע שהיא אבידה היה מחויב בהשבתה בלא שום הגבהה אם הוא יודע של מי הוא — דכיון שהוא משתמר קצת לא יתייאשו הבעלים — היכא דהגביה הוי מחויב בשמירתה מספק — לרבה הוי שומר חנם, ולרב יוסף שומר שכר — עד שתבא ליד הבעלים. ולא דמי לזקן ואינה לפי כבודו, דאמר רבה בפרקין: הכישה נתחייב בה, ואמרינן בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פח.): אימור דאמר רבה בבעלי חיים, דאנקטינהו נגרי ברייתא, אבל בשאר דברים לא — היינו משום דזקן לא מיחייב בהשבה כלל, ולכך כי יחזיר למקומה אינו חייב בשמירתה. וכן צלוחית דפרק הספינה (בבא בתרא דף פז:) לא ליחייב כלל בנטילה, דאבידה מדעת היא ואינו חייב כלל בהשבתה. אבל הכא, אם היה יודע שהיא אבידה, היה חייב ליקחנה ולהשיבה לבעלים אם היה יודע של מי הם; עתה שהוא ספק, אם הגביה — חייב בשמירתה כדין אבידה ממש. וכן משמע בפרק הספינה (שם), דקאמר צלוחית אבידה מדעת היא; משמע דאם לא היתה אבידה מדעת, א"ש דמחייב בנטילתה. ועובדא דירושלמי, דקאמר דאימור אתא מריה ולא אשכחיה, מיירי שמצאו במקום שמשתמר לגמרי, שלא היתה אבידה ואינה בת השבה, ולכך אי לא הוה לן למיחש לאתא מריה, יחזיר שפיר. וכן משמע, דסתם חפיסה יש בו סימן, ואי לא הוה משתמר לגמרי, א"כ שפיר עשה שנטלה, ואמאי אמר דלאו יאות עבד? וכן הא דתניא לקמן (בבא מציעא דף לא.): "מצא טלית או קורדום בצד גדר — אין זו אבידה ולא יגע בו, אפילו יש בו סימן", מיירי במקום המשתמר, אי נמי התם לדעת הונח שם, ולא יגע בו אפילו יש בו סימן, דדרך פועלים שמניחים טליתן או קורדומם בצד גדר של אותה שדה. ולפירוש רש"י, דפירש דלא יחזיר דליכא איניש דיהיב סימנא, קשה: דפשיטא דלא יחזירנו לשום אדם שאינו יודע מי הם הבעלים, כיון שאין בו סימן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 25b:8:2.english: And if he took [it], he shall not return [it] - There is [an authority] who explains that this applies specifically when he took it and brought it to his house, for there is concern that perhaps the owners came in the meantime and did not find what they had left there, and they will not return again to look for it; therefore, he should not return [it] to the place from which he took [it]. But if he took it and did not move from there, and saw that the owners did not come in the meantime, he should return [it]. And similarly, there is an incident in the Yerushalmi concerning Rabbi Abba bar Zavda himself, as it says: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda found wine covered in a pouch and took it. He came and asked in the study hall; they said to him, "You did not act properly." He said to them, "Shall I return it?" They said to him, "No, perhaps its owner came and did not find it, and despaired of [recovering] it." However, "if he took [it], he shall not return [it]" implies merely that he took it, and even though he did not bring it anywhere, he shall not return [it]. Rather, one can explain that [the Gemara] is speaking here of an uncertain lost item, where even if the owners left it there intentionally, it appears that they forgot it — for it is speaking of [an item] that is only slightly guarded, similar to the Mishnah, as Rabbi Abba is referring to the Mishnah. And therefore "if he took [it], he shall not return [it]," because now it is a lost item and the owners have forgotten it; and since if he had known that it was a lost item he would have been obligated to return it without any act of lifting if he knew whose it was — since, as it is slightly guarded, the owners will not despair [of recovering it] — once he lifted it, he becomes obligated in its safekeeping out of doubt — according to Rabbah he is an unpaid bailee, and according to Rav Yosef a paid bailee — until it comes into the hand of the owners. And this is not comparable to [the case of] an elder where it is not in accordance with his dignity, regarding which Rabbah said in our chapter: "[If] he struck it, he becomes obligated for it," and we say in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 88a): "Say that Rabbah stated [this] regarding living creatures, since he accustomed them to external steps [i.e., to stray], but regarding other things, no" — that is because an elder is not obligated in returning [it] at all, and therefore when he returns [it] to its place, he is not liable for its safekeeping. And similarly [regarding] the flask of [the chapter] HaSefinah (Bava Batra 87b), he is [not] obligated at all by taking [it], because it is a willful loss and he is not obligated at all in returning it. Here, however, if he had known that it was a lost item, he would have been obligated to take it and return it to the owners if he knew whose it was; now that it is uncertain, if he lifted [it], he is obligated in its safekeeping, like the law of an actual lost item. And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaSefinah (ibid.), where it says [that] a flask is a willful loss; this implies that if it were not a willful loss, it works out well that he is obligated by taking it. And the incident in the Yerushalmi, where it says that "perhaps its owner came and did not find it," is speaking of [a case] where he found it in a place that is completely guarded, so that it was not a lost item and is not subject to return; and therefore, if we did not have to be concerned that its owner came, he could properly return [it]. And so it is implied, for an ordinary pouch has an identifying mark, and if it were not completely guarded, then he acted properly in taking it — so why did [the study hall] say that he did not act properly? And similarly, that which is taught later (Bava Metzia 31a): "[If] one found a cloak or an axe alongside a fence, this is not a lost item and he shall not touch it, even if it has an identifying mark" — this is speaking of a guarded place; alternatively, there it was placed there intentionally, and he shall not touch it even if it has an identifying mark, because it is the way of laborers to leave their cloaks or axes alongside the fence of that field. And according to Rashi's explanation, who explained that "he shall not return [it]" [means] because there is no one who can give an identifying mark, [this is] difficult: for it is obvious that he should not return it to any person when he does not know who the owners are, since it has no identifying mark.
